newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador students expect 300,000 in protest march.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador students expect 300,000 in protest march.

text.p: Ecuadoran university students were counting on a turnout of 300,000 at a national march Thursday afternoon to protest economic cutbacks by the government.
Hundreds of students were congregating at university campuses in the capital of Quito and in the city of Cuenca, gathering for the march scheduled for later in the afternoon.

Although students promised the protests would be peaceful, since they started at the beginning of the week 20 students and nine policemen have been injured in stone-throwing incidents and 150 have been detained.
Pedro Salas, head of Quito's trolleybus service, told Reuters services were partially cancelled in anticipation of the march.
"We have suspended services on some routes because the students are gathering to start the protests which will be a bit more aggressive than in previous days," Sales said.

He said a trolleybus station had been attacked on Wednesday night and windows had been broken. "I hope the attack was by vandals and not the students because at the other stations we have had protests there have been no problems," said Sales.
The students are fighting the decision by President Abdala Bucaram to decree rises in electricity rates of 235 percent for homes, 77 percent for shops and 53 percent for industries.
Ecuador's trade unions are mulling a general strike for Feb 5 to protest the tariff rises.
